visit.trail_note: Rugged 4x4 trail with creek crossings; no paved road, gift shop or parking lot at the tower, per a travel article.

corrections.why: The Forest Service's 2009 project for the same mountain uses Kiamichi. Kiamachi is an older spelling used on the Forest Lookouts site.
G is not an agency name, and the Forest Lookouts page gives no key for it. The travel article places the Honobia tower in the Ouachita National Forest; identity with this record is not confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three names appear for the Whitesboro-area tower: Kiamachi Mountain (Forest Lookouts record), Honobia Fire Tower (travel article) and Kiamichi Lookout Tower (tourism listing). No source read ties them together, so the identity is unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Identity is the main problem. The Forest Lookouts record (Kiamachi Mountain, 34.6265, -94.812) is tied only by name and rough location to the Whitesboro-area steel tower that the travel article calls Honobia and the listing calls Kiamichi Lookout Tower. Treat facts as provisional until someone confirms the same tower. Facebook posts (not readable here) say a Kiamichi fire tower was built in 1927; I did not use that claim. The travel article says the tower is listed as a historical landmark; I did not verify that and left it out. The 2009 Corps guyed-tower replacement on Kiamichi Mountain (3 miles SW of Big Cedar) may or may not be the same tower; the project page does not link it to a lookout. Access was not checked against a Forest Service closure notice. Record agency G has no key on the Forest Lookouts site.
